entries.title: High-speed train crash kills at least 68 people in Spain
entries.snippet: The crash, between a moving train and another that was stopped further up the track, was caused by an "inexplicable" error, the transport minister said.

entries.title: Bloodied, dazed and angry - how passengers' rail journey turned to disaster in Spain
entries.snippet: Survivors of the train crash in Spain have spoken of their shock, panic and anger at the accident in Toledo province on Wednesday.

entries.title: Flávio Bolsonaro denies fleeing Brazil after landing in Miami
entries.snippet: The defeated Brazilian candidate claims to be the victim of a coup d’état and political persecution, recycling unsubstantiated allegations of “electoral fraud”.

entries.title: Netanyahu's bloc leading Israel election but short of majority, partial results show
entries.snippet: With 85% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's Likud party and its allies are set to win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset.

entries.title: How could Israel break election deadlock? Here are four scenarios
entries.snippet: With 85% of votes counted, all signs point to an impasse. The most likely outcome may be new elections.

entries.title: Girl seriously injured in wolf attack at German wildlife park
entries.snippet: The eight-year-old was in an enclosure with other children and a staff member when she was attacked.

entries.title: Luxury cruise passengers stranded in Cambodia due to soaring fuel costs
entries.snippet: The Villa Vie Odyssey suspended its voyage and is working with passengers on "temporary living arrangements".

entries.title: Death of US actress Hayden Panettiere ruled accidental, ending local police probe
entries.snippet: The Heroes and Nashville star died in August from the toxic effects of fentanyl, Xanax and several other drugs.

entries.title: Serbian shot dead after attacking officer outside Israeli embassy, minister says
entries.snippet: Authorities say the attacker in Belgrade was an underage male who was being monitored by security services.

entries.title: Tanzania celebrates first natural gas discovery in more than 10 years
entries.snippet: The energy minister described it as a "major milestone" for the East African nation.

entries.title: Anger in Kenya over extradition hearing delay for ex-British soldier accused of murdering woman
entries.snippet: No official reason has been given for postponing next month’s hearing to May 2027, the family says.

entries.title: Ceasefire extended across Ukraine's Kherson region, officials say
entries.snippet: The truce was originally planned for the stranded residents of Oleshky, and Russia and Ukraine say no breaches have been reported.

entries.title: King acknowledges 'suffering of the past' as Caribbean tour begins
entries.snippet: The King is on a nine-day tour that will take him to three countries, including the Bahamas, Guyana and Antigua and Barbuda.

entries.title: Dutch zookeeper dies after being mauled by leopard
entries.snippet: The woman began her career at the park when she was 17 and had worked there on-and-off for four decades.

entries.title: Norway and Finland leaders hold rare call with Putin
entries.snippet: An end to the conflict in Ukraine "will not be achieved through silence," Finland's President Alexander Stubb said.

entries.title: Lula's comeback in Brazil dents Trump's ambitions for Latin America
entries.snippet: The Trump-Lula relationship may have thawed, but several issues could reignite tensions between the two leaders.

entries.title: Ex-wife of Zimbabwe's vice-president freed after collapse of attempted murder case
entries.snippet: Marry Mubaiwa had been held on remand for seven years after being charged in 2019 for her then husband's attempted murder.

entries.title: Watch: King dances in the streets of the Bahamas capital
entries.snippet: The monarch is in the Bahamas as part of a tour of the Caribbean during which he addressed the "great suffering of the past".

entries.title: Watch: At the scene of Spain's deadly train crash
entries.snippet: People have been killed after a Spanish high-speed train collided with another train south of the capital Madrid, making this the country's worst disaster since 2013.

entries.title: Israel's election result is messy - here's why
entries.snippet: Despite having the highest voter turnout in nearly three decades, Israel's elections have had no clear winner. What does this mean for the country, asks the BBC's Yolande Knell.

entries.title: Trump administration will allow pharmacies to make popular peptides
entries.snippet: The Department of Health and Human Services will let small compounding pharmacies make six peptides that haven't been approved by the Food and Drug Administration. It may not be enough to meet demand.

entries.title: Brazilian political drama unfolds as defeated Flavio Bolsonaro arrives in Miami
entries.snippet: Defeated presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro and his family have arrived in the U.S. after Brazilian authorities ordered him to surrender his passport. He is facing multiple investigations in Brazil.

entries.title: Trump administration wants to remove regulations on a super planet-heating gas
entries.snippet: The Trump administration wants to undo a Biden-era rule that would reduce methane emissions from the oil and gas industry.

entries.title: New book revisits the 2023 killing of an unhoused man in crisis on the NYC subway
entries.snippet: Jordan Neely was frightening fellow passengers. A former Marine named Daniel Penny put Neely into a chokehold, killing him. Journalist Anand Giridharadas investigates the incident in Man in the Mirror.

entries.title: Fed holds interest rates steady even as inflation remains stubborn
entries.snippet: The Federal Reserve opted to leave its benchmark interest rate unchanged — but investors widely expect the central bank to raise rates at its next meeting in December to combat stubborn inflation.

entries.title: Dolores Huerta, influential labor leader, feminist and civil rights icon, dies at 96
entries.snippet: Huerta co-founded the United Farm Workers union to improve working conditions in the nation's fruit and vegetable fields and coined the phrase "Sí, se puede!" that became a widespread rallying cry.

entries.title: What's gone up even faster than gas or rent? The cost of caregiving
entries.snippet: A new study from AARP shows caregivers' out-of-pocket costs rose about 60% in the last five years.

entries.title: Israel's election too close to call. And, the Ebola outbreak reaches grim milestone
entries.snippet: Israeli voters turned out in record numbers, and the results remain too close to call. And, more than 10,000 people have been infected with Ebola since the outbreak was first declared in May.

entries.title: Dozens are dead in a high-speed train crash in Spain
entries.snippet: The toll is rising after a high-speed train between slammed into the rear of another train that had stopped south of Madrid, derailing two cars. It was Spain's second major train accident this year.

entries.title: How a lifelong Republican came to lead the data center battle in Ohio
entries.snippet: In Ohio, many people are displeased with the state's rapid buildout of data centers. It's a hot issue in the midterms, as political candidates from both parties try to ease voter concerns.

entries.title: King Charles III can't escape Britain's role in slavery as he tours Caribbean nations
entries.snippet: Facing demands that Britain apologize and pay reparations, palace officials say Charles will reiterate previous comments that slavery was an "atrocity that forever stains our history," while stopping short of an apology.

entries.title: Russell Brand denies all charges as he testifies at his rape and sex assault trial
entries.snippet: The British actor-comedian acknowledged in a London court on Wednesday that he had been obsessed with sex as a younger man, but denied multiple charges of rape and sexual assault, saying the claims have had a "devastating" impact on his life.

entries.title: Trump calls for prosecution of Alaska Senate candidate Peltola over Sullivan name controversy
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump called for the criminal prosecution of the Democratic candidate running for Senate in Alaska on Wednesday after revelations that her campaign appeared to be involved in recruiting a candidate with the same name as Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan.

entries.title: New polls suggest surprising Democratic gains in red-state Senate races
entries.snippet: President Trump headed to Ohio to rally voters in a race that could determine control of the Senate. That stop comes after dueling rallies in another key state offered a snapshot of the divisions shaping the midterm elections. Liz Landers reports.

entries.title: UN condemns U.S. economic embargo of Cuba though more nations sit out amid Trump push
entries.snippet: The U.N. General Assembly condemned the U.S. economic embargo of Cuba for the 34th year on Wednesday, even as Washington's campaign to influence the outcome led to a number of countries voting against the resolution or sitting out the decision for the first time.

entries.title: What's next for Israel after election produces political gridlock

entries.title: Shock, anger and mourning in Spain after 2nd major train crash this year
entries.snippet: There is shock, anger and mourning in Spain after the second fatal train crash this year. At least 68 people have died in what is now the deadliest collision there in more than a decade. William Brangham reports.

entries.title: News Wrap: Fed holds interest rates unchanged as inflation remains elevated
entries.snippet: In our news wrap Wednesday, the Federal Reserve held interest rates unchanged even as officials acknowledged that inflation remains elevated, the federal judge overseeing the prosecution of former Venezuelan president Nicolas Maduro died at the age of 92 and hundreds of passenger

entries.title: Where key Senate races stand in the final days of campaigning
entries.snippet: The race for the Senate has moved from off-the-radar a year ago to a dramatic, hard-to-predict finish where Democrats stand a chance of retaking the chamber. The contest will come down to just over a dozen races across the country. Lisa Desjardins takes a look at the map and what

entries.title: Democratic and GOP strategists assess midterm landscape in final week
entries.snippet: To discuss how the midterm races are shaping up in the final days, Amna Nawaz sat down with Democratic strategist Mo Elleithee and Republican strategist Doug Heye.

entries.title: How the Associated Press tracks and calls races on Election Night
entries.snippet: Nearly 40 million votes have already been cast for races that will determine not only who controls Congress, but also governors, mayors and city councils. For many years, PBS News has relied on the Associated Press to keep track of results, and we will again next Tuesday. Deema Z

entries.title: America's long history of gerrymandering and its role in this year's midterms
entries.snippet: Following partisan battles over political maps, nearly 35 million Americans will vote in congressional districts redrawn ahead of this year's midterms. As the nation marks its 250th anniversary, Judy Woodruff explores the origins of gerrymandering and why this centuries-old pract

entries.title: Remembering pioneering labor leader and civil rights icon Dolores Huerta
entries.snippet: Dolores Huerta, the pioneering labor leader and civil rights icon, died Wednesday from cancer at her home in Bakersfield, California. Amna Nawaz looks back at Huerta's life and legacy.

entries.title: WATCH: Trump calls for Peltola to drop out after report her campaign helped recruit 2nd Dan Sullivan
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump called for Mary Peltola to leave Alaska's Senate race and be prosecuted on Wednesday.

entries.title: Alvin Hellerstein, federal judge who handled cases on Trump, Maduro and 9/11, dies at 92
entries.snippet: Just two weeks ago, Hellerstein presided over the arraignment of former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and Maduro's wife, Cilia Flores, on torture charges that were added to their ongoing narco-terrorism conspiracy case.

entries.title: AP report: FDA scientists opposed the Trump administration's move to ease peptides access

entries.title: 4 takeaways from Israel's inconclusive election
entries.snippet: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is down but not out.

entries.title: American taxpayers' bill for Iran war grows to estimated $47.1 billion
entries.snippet: The Republican president has said new strikes on Iran are an option after the midterms and is sending more military resources to the Middle East, despite initially promising Americans a military campaign that would last only a matter of weeks.

entries.title: WATCH LIVE: Obama stumps for Ossoff and Bottoms at Georgia midterm rally
entries.snippet: Former President Barack Obama, the last Democratic president to serve two terms, is increasingly campaigning for his party, acting as a foil to President Donald Trump.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: How do the US midterms work, and why are they so important for Trump's presidency?
entries.snippet: US voters are electing a new Congress. The results will be decisive for the future of the United States, and a judgment on Donald Trump's second term as president.

entries.title: Evacuation from Oleshky: How are preparations going?
entries.snippet: A lawyer with the Save Ukraine Foundation, Myroslava Kharchenko, told DW about what has been happening in Russian-occupied Oleshky since a temporary ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump took effect.

entries.title: One year on, families seek justice after election violence
entries.snippet: One year after Tanzania's deadly post-election violence, families are still seeking answers. A government inquiry recorded 518 deaths. DW research has documented apparent use of excessive force by security forces.

entries.title: What would a new Israeli government mean for Arab neighbors? More of the same is expected, with some small positives predicted.
entries.snippet: A new Israeli government is unlikely to bring big changes on controversial topics like Palestinian statehood and Israeli troops in Lebanon and Syria, experts say. Some small positives may be possible though.

entries.title: Ukraine's Zelenskyy irked by US-Russia-China summit
entries.snippet: Volodymyr Zelenskyy has voiced his concerns about a probable meeting between the leaders of the US, China and Russia next month. Plus, a localized truce appeared to be holding in the town of Oleshky.

entries.title: Spanish train crash leaves 68 dead, PM Sanchez declares 3 days of mourning
entries.snippet: Two high-speed trains carrying hundreds of passengers collided south of Madrid. Spain's transport minister said one of the trains was told to continue its journey despite a "red signal" being in effect. Follow DW.

entries.title: Is Iran headed to war or peace after Mecca alliance meeting?
entries.snippet: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey have taken their latest peace push directly to Tehran. Officially, it was to avert a new military escalation, but their diplomatic outreach can also be seen as a warning to Iran.

entries.title: Gen Z protests in Germany: Is France-style violence looming?
entries.snippet: Young people in Germany will take to the streets this weekend to demand education and action on climate change. Politicians warn that the protests could become violent, as in France, but the situations are different.

entries.title: Israel election: Netanyahu-led bloc in slight lead with more than 80% of votes counted
entries.snippet: While partial results show the pro-Netanyahu bloc ahead of the anti-Netanyahu bloc, the final tally could take days. Neither grouping is expected to win a majority, with tough coalition talks ahead. Follow DW.

entries.title: Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?
entries.snippet: Seagrass protects coasts, shelters thousands of species and stores CO2. But some 30% of this valuable ecosystem has disappeared since the late 19th century. Can we bring it back?

entries.title: EU's 'Made in Europe' push unnerves global auto suppliers
entries.snippet: In shielding Europe's carmakers from Chinese rivals, the EU risks hurting close partners from Turkey and Morocco to Japan and South Korea. Billions in trade and hundreds of thousands of European jobs are at stake.

entries.title: Germany news: Parties debate who should succeed President Steinmeier, with several women under discussion
entries.snippet: Germany's political parties are weighing possible successors to President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, with no candidate agreed yet. Meanwhile, a poll suggests most Germans are giving Halloween a miss this year.

entries.title: Russia in Africa: What is Putin hoping to achieve?
entries.snippet: Following its invasion of Ukraine and the resulting rift with the West, Russia has declared that it intends to make a "historic return" to Africa. What have we seen of this so far?

entries.title: Dozens of people killed after high-speed trains collide in central Spain
entries.snippet: At least 68 people have been killed in a train crash in central Spain, local authorities have confirmed. Rail services between Madrid and Seville have been suspended.

entries.title: Africa's first Youth Olympics open in Senegal amid hope and scrutiny
entries.snippet: Senegal is hosting Africa's first Youth Olympics, with 2,700 young athletes competing in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. The Games bring pride and hope, but also questions over cost, rights and legacy.

entries.title: Serbian police shoot dead assailant at Israeli Embassy
entries.snippet: A "minor" has been killed by police after attacking a guard at Israel's embassy in Belgrade with knives, the interior minister says. Ivica Dacic said police had declared the highest terror alert after the incident.

entries.title: India news: Cyclone Arnab turns deadly after landfall
entries.snippet: Cyclone Arnab killed at least three people in Andhra Pradesh after making landfall earlier today. Also, a new report says India is paying a steep economic cost over heat. Follow live.

entries.title: Experts urge 'global health emergency' as climate harms accelerate
entries.snippet: A new Lancet report reveals the growing toll of climate change on human health, from rising heat deaths and drought to food insecurity and lost livelihoods.

entries.title: Egypt orders closure of independent news site Mada Masr
entries.snippet: Editor-in-chief Lina Attalah was briefly detained and fined over licensing violations. Rights groups condemned the ruling as a major blow to press freedom in Egypt, where independent media face growing pressure.
